q1_issues.issue: "Twilight and her friends" is given the collective shape - two `Agent` atoms on one `stop` event - although "stop" is not a reciprocal/aggregate predicate and no "together"/"jointly" marker is present, so the distributive default calls for one event per conjunct.
Same collective-vs-distributive deviation repeated on the `recover` event, where the two agents are copied in from the same coordinated controller.

q2_gaps: the implicit subject of a purpose to-infinitive - the connective rule says to reify both clauses and emit `(To <main> <purpose>)` but never states whether the purpose event inherits the main clause's agent, which is what the parse assumed here
notes: The object-control routing is right (complement reified at top level, attached by `Theme`, no tense of its own, controller copied in as its `Agent`), as are the possessed-plural group for "her friends" and the part-whole reading of "the elements of harmony"; a consequence worth noting is that the invitees get no role on the matrix `invite` event, so "who was invited?" cannot bind. Text is garbled in the source and was parsed as best it can be, which the instruction set directs.
